title: Variations in the Σ<SUB>SFR</SUB> ‒ Σ<SUB>mol</SUB> ‒ Σ<SUB>⋆</SUB> plane across galactic environments in PHANGS galaxies
question: Test the universality of the 2D star-forming plane relating star formation rate surface density, stellar mass surface density, and molecular gas surface density across different galactic environments at 150 pc spatial resolution.

data.sensitivity: molecular gas surface density maps have a typical uncertainty of ~1.2 M_sun pc^-2 at 150 pc resolution

what.value: Global galaxy parameters, distances, and orientations

evidence.quote: Our sample is summarized in Table [\[tab:sample\]](#tab:sample) where we use the global parameters from (cite: Leroy2021b), which leveraged the distance compilation of (cite: Anand2021) and the galaxy orientations determined by (cite: Lang2020).

what.value: Morphological environmental masks (disks, spiral arms, rings, bars, centers)

evidence.quote: We used the environmental masks described in (cite: Querejeta2021) to morphologically classify the different environments of each galaxy and label them as disks, spiral arms, rings, bars and centers.

recipe.goal: Derive molecular gas surface density maps from PHANGS-ALMA CO(2-1) products
recipe.method: Use PHANGS-ALMA v4.0 broad-masked CO(2-1) integrated intensity maps, apply S/N > 1 cut at native resolution, and convert to molecular gas mass surface density using a metallicity-dependent alpha_CO prescription and a fixed CO(2-1)-to-CO(1-0) ratio.
key_parameters: S/N cut > 1 for ALMA CO intensity
assumptions: alpha_CO = 4.35 (Z / Z_sun)^(-1.6) M_sun pc^-2 (K km s^-1)^-1

recipe.goal: Construct stellar mass surface density maps from VLT MUSE cubes
recipe.method: Correct MUSE mosaics for Milky Way extinction, Voronoi bin to S/N ~ 35 in 5300-5500 A, fit SSP templates in 4850-7000 A using pPXF within the PHANGS-MUSE DAP, reconstruct stellar mass maps from template weights, and mask foreground star velocity outliers.
key_parameters: Voronoi bin minimum S/N ~ 35 in 5300-5500 Angstrom
Fitting wavelength range 4850-7000 Angstrom with 13 logarithmically spaced ages and 6 metallicity bins
assumptions: Cardelli et al. (1989) Milky Way extinction law and Calzetti et al. (2000) extragalactic attenuation law
eMILES templates with Chabrier (2003) IMF and BaSTI isochrones

recipe.goal: Construct star formation rate surface density maps from VLT MUSE emission lines
recipe.method: Fit single Gaussian profiles to emission lines in each pixel, deredden Halpha using Balmer decrement, remove AGN/LINER pixels via BPT diagram, remove and spatially redistribute DIG emission using [S II]/Halpha, apply S/N cuts, and convert corrected Halpha flux to SFR.
key_parameters: S/N > 3 for Halpha and S/N > 1 for Hbeta; pixels with C_HII <= 0 or Halpha_obs/Hbeta_obs < 2.86 treated as nondetections
assumptions: Case B recombination Halpha_corr / Hbeta_corr = 2.86 (T = 10^4 K, n_e = 100 cm^-3) and O'Donnell (1994) extinction law (k_alpha = 2.52, k_beta = 3.66, R_V = 3.1)
Calzetti (2013) SFR calibration: SFR / (M_sun yr^-1) = 5.5e-42 Halpha_corr / (erg s^-1), scaled to a Kroupa (2001) universal IMF

recipe.goal: Match spatial resolution, rebin across spatial scales, correct for inclination, and apply environmental masks and detection fraction cuts
recipe.method: Convolve maps to common 150 pc resolution, rebin MUSE and ALMA maps to 150, 200, 300, 500, and 1000 pc pixels, apply cos(i) inclination correction, classify pixels into environments (disk, spiral arm, bar, ring, center) using Querejeta et al. (2021) masks, and restrict each environment to Sigma_* bins where both Sigma_SFR and Sigma_mol have > 60% detection fraction.
key_parameters: Pixel sizes: 150 pc (fiducial), 200 pc, 300 pc, 500 pc, 1 kpc
Detection fraction threshold > 60% per Sigma_* bin, applied independently per environment (removes ~20% of all 150 pc pixels, ~38% of disk pixels, <5% of other environments)
assumptions: Inclination correction factor cos(i) using galaxy inclinations from Lang et al. (2020)

recipe.goal: Fit the 2D star-forming plane across galactic environments using hierarchical Bayesian linear regression and compare against 1D rKS model
recipe.method: Center log Sigma_SFR, log Sigma_*, and log Sigma_mol by fixed full-sample means and fit log Sigma_SFR,i = C_*,i log Sigma_* + C_mol,i log Sigma_mol + C_norm using hierarchical Bayesian linear regression in PyMC3 with a single common C_norm and intrinsic scatter sigma_intr across environments. Compare 2D plane model to 1D rKS model using leave-one-out (LOO) cross-validation.
key_parameters: 4 MCMC chains, 2000 iterations + 2000 burn-in iterations per chain, NUTS sampler
assumptions: Single normalization C_norm and common intrinsic dispersion sigma_intr across all environments

recipe.goal: Correlate single-galaxy environmental plane slopes with local physical and stellar population parameters
recipe.method: Select 8 galaxies satisfying environmental and detection criteria, fit C_*, C_mol, and C_norm per environment within each galaxy, compute environmental averages of 13 physical parameters, and compute the overall average weighted Pearson correlation coefficient <rho> with 50 Monte Carlo perturbations for uncertainties.
key_parameters: Galaxy selection criteria: >= 3 environments, has bar and spiral arms, < 50% pixels removed by detection threshold (yields 8 galaxies with log M_* >= 10.6)
50 Monte Carlo simulations per galaxy for correlation uncertainty
assumptions: Typical stellar scale height h_* = 300 pc for free-fall time calculation; atomic gas neglected in mid-plane hydrostatic pressure P_h

score_reason: The Bayesian hierarchical model (equations, centering constants, hyperpriors, priors, sampler, chain counts) and physical prescriptions (alpha_CO, R_21, SFR conversion, extinction laws, S/N cuts) are documented in detail, and PHANGS-ALMA v4.0 products and Querejeta+2021 masks are public. However, the analysis scripts and exact Sigma_* cut boundaries for each environment are not released with the paper.
rediscovery_reason: Uses public PHANGS-ALMA DR1 (v4.0) CO(2-1) maps, environmental masks, and PHANGS-MUSE data products, provides explicit equations, priors, and centering constants for the PyMC3 regression, and reports exact numerical slopes and pixel counts per environment in Table 2 as an answer key.
